ground_truth.unit: log points of annualised household electricity consumption (kWh)
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Effect of the Reform on Residential Electricity Consumption and Expenditure (2011-2014)"), column (1), row Reform (T): the paper's difference-in-differences estimate of the August 2013 Spanish electricity pricing reform (fixed charge raised, regulated volumetric rate cut) on household electricity consumption, estimated by OLS.  Data: Spanish Household Budget Survey households interviewed between August 2011 and April 2014, each interviewed twice, in the same two-week period of two consecutive years; the control group has both interviews before the reform, the treated group its second interview after it.  T is the post-reform dummy for interviews whose electricity bill falls under the reform (the paper places the response one month after the reform, when households receive a reformed bill).  Dependent variable: log of electricity consumption in the month before the interview (kWh, annualised by the survey).  Regressors: T, log household price per kWh (expenditure divided by consumption), log income and its square, months since reform, and controls for household size, number of rooms, dwelling surface, elderly members, education of the household head, household economic situation (number of economically active members), renting, building older than 25 years, municipality-size dummies, urban area, province capital, regional dummies, quarterly dummies and year fixed effects.  No household fixed effects.  Standard errors clustered at the household level.

i4r.notes: Team 49 blanket verdict (code reproduces the paper's output); no meta-database row for column 1.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=-0.134095 vs claimed=-0.178 (relative error 24.67%, tolerance 15.17%, the ±1·SE band with SE=0.027).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: LIML implemented by hand as a k-class estimator (fixest has only 2SLS); FE-LIML applies it to within-household demeaned data; household-clustered sandwich SEs.

Instruments are the provided gap-filled deflated log effective prices lnPRE_papas_, lnPRE_aguav_, lnPRE_gascar_ (the unfilled versions would cut N to ~10,300, inconsistent with the paper's equal N across columns). The LIML price coefficients do not match the paper, so the instrument construction likely differs.
Price regressor is the deflated log kWh price lnPRE (nominal lnp_kwh makes the expenditure and consumption reform coefficients identical, which the paper's are not).
Treated-group dummy D (Tm) included in the pooled (non-FE) models; absorbed under household FE.
cell.notes: Sample: rows with non-missing T2 (the Aug 2011-Apr 2014 two-interview panel, 25,775 obs, matching the paper), then complete cases on regression variables -> 20,872 obs, 10,729 households (both match Table 2 exactly). Reform (T) = T2; months since reform = dist; controls: ln income and its square, household size, rooms, square metres, elderly present, building >25y, renting, urban, province capital, education, employment-situation, municipality-size, region and quarter dummies, year FE. Price elasticities match (-1.043 vs -1.044 OLS; -1.033 vs -1.026 FE); FE consumption effect -0.166 vs -0.154; OLS effects (-0.134, -0.139) smaller in magnitude than claimed; IV/LIML columns and the FE expenditure effect do not reproduce well. Attempts 2 and 3 were the same exploratory script as attempt 4; they hung because the Docker daemon was wedged (containers stuck in Created), produced no output, and were killed; Docker was restarted by the coordinator. Attempt 4 is the successful exploratory run. Readme.pdf in the mount was read (data provenance only); the dofiles folder was empty; no scripts were opened.
